# Freedom to refuse, and the ability God gives


The strongest objection to sola gratia comes from the Arminian side, and it is
an objection from Scripture. Stephen told the council, "you always resist the
Holy Spirit" (Acts 7:51). Paul tells believers, "do not grieve the Holy Spirit of
God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption" (Ephesians 4:30), and
"do not quench the Spirit" (1 Thessalonians 5:19). Jesus says that "the
blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven … either in this age or in
the age to come" (Matthew 12:31–32). If the Spirit can be resisted, grieved and
quenched, and if one sin against him is never forgiven, then surely the grace he
brings can be refused.

## What the texts settle, and what they do not

Every party grants what the texts say. Dort says that believers "grieve the Holy
Spirit" (V, article 5); Calvin, on Ephesians 4:30, that "we grieve him when we
do not follow his guidance"; the Formula of Concord, that "those who always
resist the Holy Ghost … are not converted". So the step from the texts to "the
Spirit's work is resisted" is rated `consensus`.

The dispute is the next step, from resistance to the claim that the grace that
saves can be *finally* refused. "Resist" has two senses. A person can resist for
a time and be overcome, which the Reformed say happens to the elect before they
believe, and to believers when they grieve the Spirit and are brought back. Or a
person can refuse to the end. Only the second sense denies sola gratia, and
each route to it needs a reading of its own:

- **Acts 7:51**, read as resistance to the grace that saves, as the Remonstrants
  read it. The Reformed say that what Stephen's hearers resisted was the
  outward call of the preached word.
- **Ephesians 4:30**, read with the Formula of Concord: those who obstinately
  resist "do not receive, but grieve and lose, the Holy Ghost". Dort denies the
  reading: God "does not wholly withdraw the Holy Spirit from his own people,
  even in their melancholy falls".
- **Matthew 12:31–32**, read with Augustine: the sin never forgiven is
  impenitence to the end, "the persevering hardness of an impenitent heart".
  Calvin rejects the reading outright ("Those who define it to be impenitence
  may be refuted without any difficulty") and takes the sin to be knowing
  contempt of the Spirit, which the regenerate "cannot possibly fall into". And
  the step from Augustine's reading to final refusal of *saving* grace is rated
  `disputed`, because Augustine himself holds both that reading and that God is
  the one "whom no man's will resists when He wills to give salvation".

Grieving the Spirit is Paul's word, and it is addressed to believers. The
unforgivable sin is Jesus' word, in the Gospels. They are kept as two texts with
two readings, because no reader cited here takes grieving to be the
unforgivable sin.

## Two positions between Dort and the Remonstrants

**The Lutherans** of the Formula of Concord (1577) are the reader the closing
step of the Reformed case did not expect. They hold that conversion is "not only
in part, but altogether an operation, gift, and present, and work of the Holy
Ghost alone", and that in it man "does nothing whatever towards it, but only
suffers what God works in him". That is the third part of sola gratia as Dort
states it. And they hold that grace can be resisted and lost, which denies the
second. So the step from "God's work alone" to "grace cannot be finally
refused" is rated `disputed`, and the Formula is why.

**Wesley** holds that "there is a measure of free-will supernaturally restored to
every man", so that each has "power either to resist or yield to the grace of
God"; that grace, which "goes before" anything a person does, he calls
"preventing grace". It is received by faith alone: "Of yourselves cometh neither
your faith nor your salvation".

## The third way

The third way, as it was put to this argument: God gives the one who hears the
gospel the ability to believe, as Adam and Eve were made able to obey or to eat
the forbidden fruit (Genesis 2:16–17); the offer of grace is real; and it is
received by faith alone. Stated that way, it is held by Dort, by the Lutherans
and by Wesley alike, and it does not decide whether the grace that saves can be
finally refused: two readings, Dort's and Arminius's, both satisfy it and
disagree about exactly that (`third_way_leaves_resistibility_open`).

What decides it is what kind of help the ability is. Augustine drew the
distinction. "The aid without which a thing does not come to pass is one thing,
and the aid by which a thing comes to pass is another." Adam was given the first,
"not that by which it should be brought about that he should persevere, but that
without which he could not of free will persevere"; the saints are given the
second, "so that by means of this gift they cannot help persevering" (*On Rebuke
and Grace*, ch. 34). Read as Adam's kind of help, the third way is Wesley's, and
it falls to Dort. Read as the saints' kind, it is Dort's, and it falls to the
Remonstrants (`whatTheAbilityIs`).

## Each position, concluding what it holds

The packages in `Packages` are asked for sola gratia. Weighed against one
another, each position concludes what it holds, as these do.

## Each position holds together

Every position weighed below has a model.

**The Lutheran position holds together, and reaches what it holds**: the

**`thirdWay_establishes`**

**The third way reaches what it says**: salvation by grace, received by
faith alone.

```lean

-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="objection_establishes"></a>
**`objection_establishes`**

**The objection from the Spirit's resistance is valid on its own grounds.**
Grant the texts of resistance and any one of its three readings, and the grace
that saves is not effectual of itself.

```lean
theorem objection_establishes : Establishes objection
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="third_way_leaves_resistibility_open"></a>
**`third_way_leaves_resistibility_open`**

**The third way leaves resistibility open.** Grant everything it says: Adam
made able to stand or fall, the ability to believe given by God, faith alone,
and that grace which can be finally refused is not effectual of itself. Whether
the grace that saves is effectual of itself neither follows nor fails. Arminius's
reading satisfies every premise and denies it; Dort's satisfies every premise and
holds it. One fact: the third way, as stated, neither blocks sola gratia nor
establishes it.

```lean
theorem third_way_leaves_resistibility_open : Independent thirdWay.premises (p
    Claim.graceIsEffectualOfItself)
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

The third way has a model: Dort's reading.

### What kind of help the ability is

<a id="asAidWithoutWhich"></a>
**`asAidWithoutWhich`**

The ability read as Adam's kind of help: it makes believing possible, and the
grace that gives it can be finally refused. Wesley's reading.

```lean
def asAidWithoutWhich : Reading Claim :=
  { name := "as the help without which a person cannot believe, Adam's kind",
    commits := p Claim.savingGraceCanBeFinallyRefused,
    source := asAidWithoutWhichSource }
```

<a id="asAidByWhich"></a>
**`asAidByWhich`**

The ability read as the saints' kind of help: the grace that gives it brings
believing about. Augustine's reading of the grace given to the saints, and
Dort's.

```lean
def asAidByWhich : Reading Claim :=
  { name := "as the help by which a person believes, the saints' kind",
    commits := p Claim.graceIsEffectualOfItself,
    source := asAidByWhichSource }
```

- (6) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}} \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\) — *would deny:* The grace that saves brings about the consent it seeks
- (7) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-14}{P_{14}} \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\) — *would give:* The grace that saves brings about the consent it seeks
- \\(\vdash\\) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-24}{P_{24}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-15}{P_{15}}\\) — *at issue:* \\(\href{claims.html#claim-24}{P_{24}}\\) Salvation is by grace and not earned: grace goes before every saving act; \\(\href{claims.html#claim-15}{P_{15}}\\) Grace is received by faith alone

</div>

Grounded in scripture alone: Romans 11:6 — if it is by grace, it is no longer on the basis of works, Genesis 2:16–17 — of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat.

<a id="thirdWayAsAidWithoutWhich_is_satisfiable"></a>
**`thirdWayAsAidWithoutWhich_is_satisfiable`**

**The first reading is fair**: the third way, read as giving Adam's kind of
help, can be held without contradiction. It is Wesley's position.

```lean
theorem thirdWayAsAidWithoutWhich_is_satisfiable : Satisfiable
    thirdWayAsAidWithoutWhich.premises
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="thirdWayAsAidByWhich_is_satisfiable"></a>
**`thirdWayAsAidByWhich_is_satisfiable`**

**The second reading is fair**: the third way, read as giving the saints'
kind of help, can be held without contradiction. It is Dort's position.

```lean
theorem thirdWayAsAidByWhich_is_satisfiable : Satisfiable
    thirdWayAsAidByWhich.premises
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="remonstrants_do_not_reach_adams_kind"></a>
**`remonstrants_do_not_reach_adams_kind`**

The Remonstrants hold together with the first reading: Arminius's reading
satisfies both.

```lean
theorem remonstrants_do_not_reach_adams_kind : Satisfiable
    (remonstrantPosition.premises ++ thirdWayAsAidWithoutWhich.premises)
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="dort_does_not_reach_the_saints_kind"></a>
**`dort_does_not_reach_the_saints_kind`**

Dort holds together with the second reading: Dort's reading satisfies both.

```lean
theorem dort_does_not_reach_the_saints_kind : Satisfiable (reformed.premises
    ++ thirdWayAsAidByWhich.premises)
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="whereAdamsKindFalls"></a>
**`whereAdamsKindFalls`**

**Why Dort stands against the third way, read as Adam's kind of help.** The
crux is Dort's step from God's work alone to grace that cannot be finally
refused, which the Lutherans dispute. With the Romans strand granted, it breaks
the reading at its three premises: the ability given, the reading of it as a
help that can be refused, and the step every party grants, that grace which can
be finally refused is not effectual of itself.

**Why *Reformed (the Canons of Dort)* stands against *The third way (an ability given, received by faith), read as the help without which a person cannot believe, Adam's kind*.**

- **The crux:** \\(\href{claims.html#claim-23}{P_{23}} \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\), a premise of *Reformed (the Canons of Dort)*.
- **What it does:** its conclusion does not follow without it.
- **Granted:** \\(\href{claims.html#claim-3}{P_{3}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-18}{P_{18}}\\), \\((\href{claims.html#claim-3}{P_{3}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-18}{P_{18}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-23}{P_{23}}\\), which the break also needs.
- **Where the rival breaks:** \\(\href{claims.html#claim-14}{P_{14}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-14}{P_{14}} \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}} \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\) cannot be held together with \\(\href{claims.html#claim-23}{P_{23}} \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\) and \\(\href{claims.html#claim-3}{P_{3}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-18}{P_{18}}\\), \\((\href{claims.html#claim-3}{P_{3}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-18}{P_{18}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-23}{P_{23}}\\); each is needed for the break, and without the crux they stand.
- **What this rests on:**
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-3}{P_{3}}\\) Romans 9:16 — it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God, who has mercy — *consensus*: Rom 9:16
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-18}{P_{18}}\\) Romans 9:16 is about God's mercy in saving, not only in choosing a people for history — *well supported*: [Arminius 1853](../../bibliography.md#arminius-works-3-1853), pp. 527–565; [Abasciano 2006](../../bibliography.md#abasciano-corporate-election-romans-9-2006), p. 351
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-23}{P_{23}}\\) Conversion is God's work alone: God regenerates, and the will does nothing to it — *disputed*: [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Canons of Dort, III/IV, arts. 10–12
  - the step itself — *consensus*: [Tanner 1990](../../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 8; [Council of Trent 1848](../../bibliography.md#waterworth-trent-1848), p. 36; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Five Arminian Articles (1610), art. 4; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Canons of Dort, III/IV, art. 10; *disputed*: [Robertson 1931](../../bibliography.md#robertson-word-pictures-4-1931), ad loc. Eph 2:8; [Calvin 1854](../../bibliography.md#calvin-galatians-ephesians-1854), pp. 228–229; *disputed*: [Arminius 1825](../../bibliography.md#arminius-works-1-1825), p. 600; [Arminius 1825](../../bibliography.md#arminius-works-1-1825), p. 681; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Five Arminian Articles (1610), art. 4; *disputed*: [Arminius 1853](../../bibliography.md#arminius-works-3-1853), pp. 527–565; *consensus*: [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), p. 593; [Calvin 1854](../../bibliography.md#calvin-galatians-ephesians-1854), p. 301; [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration II.60; *well supported*: [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration II.89; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Canons of Dort, III/IV, art. 12; *disputed*: [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration II.89; [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration II.60; [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration XI.41

<a id="whereTheSaintsKindFalls"></a>
**`whereTheSaintsKindFalls`**

**Why the Remonstrants stand against the third way, read as the saints' kind
of help.** The crux is the step every party grants, that grace which can be
finally refused is not effectual of itself. With the Remonstrants' reading of
Acts 7:51 granted, it breaks the reading at its two premises: the ability given,
and the reading of it as a help that brings believing about. The crux is cheap;
what the break rests on is the Remonstrants' reading, which Dort denies.

**Why *Remonstrant (the Five Articles, 1610)* stands against *The third way (an ability given, received by faith), read as the help by which a person believes, the saints' kind*.**

- **The crux:** \\(\href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}} \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\), a premise of *Remonstrant (the Five Articles, 1610)*.
- **What it does:** its conclusion does not follow without it.
- **Granted:** \\(\href{claims.html#claim-5}{P_{5}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-6}{P_{6}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-7}{P_{7}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-20}{P_{20}}\\), \\((\href{claims.html#claim-5}{P_{5}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-6}{P_{6}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-7}{P_{7}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-10}{P_{10}}\\), \\((\href{claims.html#claim-10}{P_{10}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-20}{P_{20}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}}\\), which the break also needs.
- **Where the rival breaks:** \\(\href{claims.html#claim-14}{P_{14}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-14}{P_{14}} \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\) cannot be held together with \\(\href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}} \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\) and \\(\href{claims.html#claim-5}{P_{5}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-6}{P_{6}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-7}{P_{7}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-20}{P_{20}}\\), \\((\href{claims.html#claim-5}{P_{5}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-6}{P_{6}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-7}{P_{7}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-10}{P_{10}}\\), \\((\href{claims.html#claim-10}{P_{10}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-20}{P_{20}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}}\\); each is needed for the break, and without the crux they stand.
- **What this rests on:**
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-5}{P_{5}}\\) Acts 7:51 — you always resist the Holy Spirit — *consensus*: Acts 7:51
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-6}{P_{6}}\\) Ephesians 4:30 — do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed — *consensus*: Eph 4:30
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-7}{P_{7}}\\) 1 Thessalonians 5:19 — do not quench the Spirit — *consensus*: 1 Thess 5:19
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-20}{P_{20}}\\) What Stephen's hearers resisted in Acts 7:51 was the grace that saves — *disputed*: [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Five Arminian Articles (1610), art. 4
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-10}{P_{10}}\\) The Holy Spirit's work is resisted, by unbelievers and by believers — *consensus*: [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), p. 593; [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration II.60
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}}\\) The grace that saves can be finally refused — *disputed*: [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Five Arminian Articles (1610), art. 4; [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration XI.41; [Wesley 1827](../../bibliography.md#wesley-works-9-1827), p. 397
  - the step itself — *consensus*: [Tanner 1990](../../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 8; [Council of Trent 1848](../../bibliography.md#waterworth-trent-1848), p. 36; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Five Arminian Articles (1610), art. 4; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Canons of Dort, III/IV, art. 10; *consensus*: [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), p. 593; [Calvin 1854](../../bibliography.md#calvin-galatians-ephesians-1854), p. 301; [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration II.60; *well supported*: [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Five Arminian Articles (1610), art. 4; [Arminius 1825](../../bibliography.md#arminius-works-1-1825), p. 600; *consensus*: [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Five Arminian Articles (1610), art. 4; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Canons of Dort, III/IV, art. 12

<a id="whatTheAbilityIs"></a>
**`whatTheAbilityIs`**

**What the ability God gives is, read both ways.** The claim is the third
way's: God gives the one who hears the gospel the ability to believe, as Adam was
made able to stand or to fall.

Read as Adam's kind of help, the help "without which" a person cannot believe,
it is Wesley's position. The Remonstrants hold it with them, and it falls to
Dort, at Dort's step from God's work alone to grace that cannot be finally
refused, which is rated `disputed` because the Lutherans grant its ground and
deny its conclusion.

Read as the saints' kind, the help "by which" a person believes, it is Dort's.
Dort holds it with it, and it falls to the Remonstrants, at their reading of
Acts 7:51, which is rated `disputed`.

Each reading is fair: the third way read either way can be held without
contradiction. Which reading its holder means is not something the dilemma
decides. What it shows is that the third way takes a side the moment it says
which kind of help God gives, and which side depends on the answer.

**Every reading of \\(\href{claims.html#claim-14}{P_{14}}\\), answered.** *The third way (an ability given, received by faith)* holds \\(\href{claims.html#claim-14}{P_{14}}\\). It is read 2 ways here, and each reading is checked; none can be left out.

**1. Read as the help without which a person cannot believe, Adam's kind.** The claim commits *The third way (an ability given, received by faith)* to \\(\href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}}\\) — so read by [Wesley 1827](../../bibliography.md#wesley-works-9-1827), p. 397; [Schaff 1887](../../bibliography.md#npnf1-05-1887), p. 485 (*disputed*).

Against *Reformed (the Canons of Dort)*, it cannot be held. Where it breaks:

**Why *Reformed (the Canons of Dort)* stands against *The third way (an ability given, received by faith), read as the help without which a person cannot believe, Adam's kind*.**

- **The crux:** \\(\href{claims.html#claim-23}{P_{23}} \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\), a premise of *Reformed (the Canons of Dort)*.
- **What it does:** its conclusion does not follow without it.
- **Granted:** \\(\href{claims.html#claim-3}{P_{3}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-18}{P_{18}}\\), \\((\href{claims.html#claim-3}{P_{3}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-18}{P_{18}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-23}{P_{23}}\\), which the break also needs.
- **Where the rival breaks:** \\(\href{claims.html#claim-14}{P_{14}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-14}{P_{14}} \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-13}{P_{13}} \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\) cannot be held together with \\(\href{claims.html#claim-23}{P_{23}} \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\) and \\(\href{claims.html#claim-3}{P_{3}}\\), \\(\href{claims.html#claim-18}{P_{18}}\\), \\((\href{claims.html#claim-3}{P_{3}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-18}{P_{18}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-23}{P_{23}}\\); each is needed for the break, and without the crux they stand.
- **What this rests on:**
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-3}{P_{3}}\\) Romans 9:16 — it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God, who has mercy — *consensus*: Rom 9:16
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-18}{P_{18}}\\) Romans 9:16 is about God's mercy in saving, not only in choosing a people for history — *well supported*: [Arminius 1853](../../bibliography.md#arminius-works-3-1853), pp. 527–565; [Abasciano 2006](../../bibliography.md#abasciano-corporate-election-romans-9-2006), p. 351
  - \\(\href{claims.html#claim-23}{P_{23}}\\) Conversion is God's work alone: God regenerates, and the will does nothing to it — *disputed*: [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Canons of Dort, III/IV, arts. 10–12
  - the step itself — *consensus*: [Tanner 1990](../../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Trent, Session VI (1547), ch. 8; [Council of Trent 1848](../../bibliography.md#waterworth-trent-1848), p. 36; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Five Arminian Articles (1610), art. 4; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Canons of Dort, III/IV, art. 10; *disputed*: [Robertson 1931](../../bibliography.md#robertson-word-pictures-4-1931), ad loc. Eph 2:8; [Calvin 1854](../../bibliography.md#calvin-galatians-ephesians-1854), pp. 228–229; *disputed*: [Arminius 1825](../../bibliography.md#arminius-works-1-1825), p. 600; [Arminius 1825](../../bibliography.md#arminius-works-1-1825), p. 681; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Five Arminian Articles (1610), art. 4; *disputed*: [Arminius 1853](../../bibliography.md#arminius-works-3-1853), pp. 527–565; *consensus*: [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), p. 593; [Calvin 1854](../../bibliography.md#calvin-galatians-ephesians-1854), p. 301; [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration II.60; *well supported*: [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration II.89; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), §Canons of Dort, III/IV, art. 12; *disputed*: [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration II.89; [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration II.60; [Concordia Triglotta 1921](../../bibliography.md#concordia-triglotta-1921), §Solid Declaration XI.41

Against *Remonstrant (the Five Articles, 1610)*, it is not reached: *Remonstrant (the Five Articles, 1610)* holds, and can be held together with it.

**2. Read as the help by which a person believes, the saints' kind.** The claim commits *The third way (an ability given, received by faith)* to \\(\href{claims.html#claim-25}{P_{25}}\\) — so read by [Schaff 1887](../../bibliography.md#npnf1-05-1887), p. 485; [Schaff 1977](../../bibliography.md#schaff-creeds-christendom-3-1977), p. 591 (*disputed*).
